items.title: Gap Mangione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: And one thing led to another. And he asked us to sit in. So Chuck and I and this friend our ours who played saxophone, Benny Salzano, who’s still in New York and still plays but not to the extent that we’ve been playing, sat in.

ctx.x: I’m a huge fan of Cannonball Adderley, so I saw that right away, and I wondered how did that come about? Was he playing in town?

Not to take up the entire time, but one time, it was a night before a New Year’s Eve, and I was old enough to drive but not old enough to have a car. But I had a girlfriend who had a car, and she was old enough to drive at night. So we were out, the night before New Year’s Eve, and heard that there was some really good music, a band, near Geneva. And that was kind of like all we really knew. So we started over toward there and ended up on Route 414, which if you look at a map is a farm road. Even now it’s not —…
Oh that is just a great story. How do you suppose they ended up in that place in the middle of nowhere?
